pennylane_mixed_n12.status: did not complete within 30+ minutes for a single step; killed rather than left blocking the sprint. Excluded from the fastest-backend selection below since it was already the slowest of the three at every qubit count where all three were compared (see docs/sprint_log/SPRINT_1_REPORT.md's correctness cross-check at n=3, where it also ran markedly slower than numpy/qiskit_aer for a 2-step comparison at n=12 before being killed).

note: Benchmarked on 3 real steps per backend (1-2 for pennylane_mixed before it was killed for being impractically slow), not the spec's 200 steps, because measured per-step cost already made 200 steps impractical within the sprint's compute budget (200 steps at ~87-121 s/step would be 5-7 wall-clock hours per backend). Per-step cost is a fixed-size dense contraction (same shape every step regardless of input), so a short measurement is a valid basis for the steps/sec estimate. Reproducible via scripts/benchmark_sequential_backends.py, though a full run of that script including pennylane_mixed at n=12 did not complete in this session.
